solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Start to devise style in office

parts.note: to open a meeting or a shop is to start it
to devise a scheme is to plan it

explanation.surface: Advice on how to begin designing the look of a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan layout, with few or no internal walls, is a familiar way of arranging a workplace.

clue.text: Yield more than rock

parts.note: out- in verbs like outdo or outrun means more than, beyond
a farm's yield is its crop

explanation.surface: A farming boast about harvesting more than something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in the reverse of the clue's order: 'more than' comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a mass of bedrock exposed above the surrounding soil.

clue.text: I make good, to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the phrase make good is used, so its letters are found inside it

explanation.surface: Someone claiming they partly make amends.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the break between 'make' and 'good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for the first-person pronoun and the psychological term for the self.

clue.text: Landed respectable neckwear given by daughter

parts.note: a proper person is respectable and decent
a tie is worn round the neck
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A respectable tie handed over by a daughter, perhaps as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Landed gentry are those owning estates, so landed means owning land or property.

clue.text: Warm approval is out of place for vetting of books

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place is taken away from the word for warm approval

parts.note: a plaudit is enthusiastic praise
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Praise is inappropriate when checking accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' reads as 'inappropriate', but 'out of' strips PL (place) from PLAUDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of an organisation's accounts.

clue.text: A small fishing boat returned every time

indicators.note: something returned comes back, so the letters of these words are read backwards

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a yawl is a small two-masted sailing boat, used for fishing

explanation.surface: A little boat that comes back to harbour without fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SYAWL round to LWAYS, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means on every occasion, without exception.

clue.text: Made up a story and was heartless

indicators.note: with its heart gone, the word loses its central letter

parts.note: to be or exist is to have lived

explanation.surface: Someone who invented a tale and behaved cruelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks like the second definition, but it removes the middle V of LIVED (was, existed).
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate a story is to tell untruths, to have been dishonest.

clue.text: Charm of rogue flanked by a couple of supporters

indicators.note: having something on either side, so one pair surrounds the other piece

parts.note: two lots of A BRA, a bra being a supporting garment
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue

explanation.surface: The appeal of a villain with two backers beside him.
explanation.walkthrough: One A BRA goes either side of CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a magic incantation, a charm spoken by conjurors.

clue.text: Walks over younger member of family

parts.note: steps are paces taken in walking
on can mean over or upon, as with a lid on a jar

explanation.surface: Someone tramples a junior relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is a spouse's son from an earlier relationship, a junior member of the household.

clue.text: Giant company supported by America admits defeat

indicators.note: lets in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second, held up by it

parts.note: US is the United States
a defeat is a loss

explanation.surface: A huge firm backed by the USA concedes it has lost.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supported by' means sitting on top of.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colossus of Rhodes was a huge statue, so the word names any giant.

clue.text: To do nothing and go back to risk regret is barely credible

indicators.note: the words do, nothing and go are read backwards together

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to bet is to risk money
to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Advice that idling and retreating only risk later remorse is hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DOOGO round to OGOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so good it seems impossible is scarcely believable, a set phrase for suspicious good fortune.

clue.text: Striking style of film, Renoir work of art is fun

indicators.note: striking out means deleting, so a word is removed from the painter's name

parts.note: film noir is a dark style of crime film
an artwork is a creation

explanation.surface: An art lover praising Renoir's arresting cinematic style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like praise but deletes NOIR from RENOIR, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreation is leisure activity done for enjoyment, an amusement.

clue.text: Bad actor vainly looking at the future

indicators.note: badly done, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poor performer gazing hopefully at the career ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant claims to see future events, so is someone seeing ahead.

clue.text: When to pen court decrees

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Asking at what time a court will write its rulings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like writing, but it means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of Parliament are laws, formal decrees.

clue.text: Sign up for the famous indecent film covering canines?

parts.note: a blue joke or movie is smutty
plaque is the film that forms on teeth, canines being teeth

explanation.surface: A notice advertising a dirty movie about dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a round sign on a building marking where a famous person lived. 'canines' are teeth here, not dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: These round wall signs are put up to commemorate notable people at houses linked to them.

clue.text: Hat comes adrift with open carriage

indicators.note: comes loose and gets disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hat blows off in an open-topped carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes HAT and OPEN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A phaeton is a light open four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Conrad's novel motors on in chaos

indicators.note: in disorder, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A book in which engines keep roaring amid mayhem.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostromo is Joseph Conrad's 1904 novel set in a South American republic.

clue.text: Old sultan's envy, perhaps, about a young man

indicators.note: around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: envy is one of the seven deadly sins
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A historic ruler's jealousy of a youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century Muslim sultan of Egypt and Syria who fought the Crusaders.

clue.text: Might piano add second instrument for gripping effect?

parts.note: might is strength or force
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a piano plus another instrument would make music more gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping effect' plays on a gripping performance; the tool literally grips.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are pincers or tongs used by surgeons to hold things firmly.

clue.text: Help to include right author

indicators.note: to contain, so the letter goes inside the word for help

parts.note: to foster is to encourage or help along

explanation.surface: Assisting to bring in the correct writer.
explanation.definitionFit: E. M. Forster was the English novelist of A Passage to India and Howards End.

clue.text: Resolved to include mint, say, in Australian beer

indicators.note: to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: someone resolved is set on a course, determined
mint is an example of a herb

explanation.surface: Deciding to add mint to an Aussie lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' reads like an anagram signal but means SET.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang the word for a fizzy sweet is used humorously for beer.

clue.text: Three changed in multiplication with about that amount

indicators.note: altered, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: by is the word used in multiplying, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A sum where three is altered within a product, giving a nearby figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns THREE into THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of the adverb means thereabouts, approximately that number.

clue.text: Fell back in space

indicators.note: the word is read backwards

parts.note: a fell is upland moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled backwards into the void.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a verb, but it is a noun for northern English hill country.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means space, as in room to move.

clue.text: Make public concert attendance around middle of July

indicators.note: these two pieces surround the letters from the month

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
the gate is the number of spectators at an event

indicators.note: the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Crowds at a summer concert in mid-July.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous London summer concert season; 'attendance' is the gate, the number of spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: To promulgate a law or idea is to proclaim it widely.

clue.text: Madness of king over leaving country

indicators.note: departing, so these letters go from the country's name

parts.note: Romania is a country in eastern Europe
R is for rex, Latin for king
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A monarch's lunacy leads to the abdication of his realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Mania is a state of wild excitement or obsession, a kind of insanity.

clue.text: Just stylishness gets left out

indicators.note: left out means omitted, so the letter is removed

parts.note: flair is style or panache

explanation.surface: Mere elegance is neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and fair both mean impartial and equitable.

clue.text: Chinese space shot means quarantine

indicators.note: shot as in broken or ruined, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Chinese rocket launch means the crew must be isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space shot' reads as a rocket launch, but 'shot' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This vast public square in central Beijing is a famous open space.

clue.text: Cunning regularly displayed by parrots

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Parrots often show their cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean craft or guile, as in artful.

clue.text: Check reversing speed in road

indicators.note: placed within, so one piece sits inside the other
reversing as a driver backs up, so the word for speed is read from its end

parts.note: rate means speed, as in rate of knots

explanation.surface: Slow down by backing up in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' sounds like driving, but it turns the word for speed round, giving ETAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard something is to delay or slow it, holding it in check.

clue.text: Records judge is for hanging

parts.note: tapes are recordings
to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: Court documents show a judge favours the death penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge' and 'hanging' suggest a court; a hanging here is a wall textile.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven fabric hung on a wall as decoration.
